title: Beatrix and the Colony
premise: Marguerite Okonkwo has spent thirty years tending Earth's abandoned seed vault, the last human link between two colonies that severed contact after a war no one will name. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew aged backward into childhood, carrying fragmented memories of a massacre on the colony Meridian, Marguerite is summoned as the only neutral witness both worlds still trust. As she reconstructs the truth from the children's fractured recollections and the vault's hidden genetic archives, she discovers her own family helped erase the massacre — and that the same faction now plans to sterilize Meridian permanently. To stop them, Marguerite must broadcast the recovered memory to both worlds, sacrificing the vault, her legacy, and finally her own life so that the truth outlives her.
about_author: Vesper Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing endangered seed collections across three continents. Their fiction explores what institutions remember when the people inside them choose to forget.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She runs her solitary maintenance circuit between the seed vault and the relay stations, establishing her routine, her loneliness, and the cold silence between Earth and Meridian. A routine supply drop arrives with an impossible message: the Halcyon is returning after forty years. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The Halcyon docks, and its crew of forty disembarks as children under ten, biologically reversed, clutching data cores they cannot explain. Medical officer Ilsa Reyes begs Marguerite, as a neutral party, to help interview them before their memories degrade further. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: What the Smallest One Saw
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Marguerite and Tam, a seven-year-old crew member. Through play therapy, Tam describes fire on Meridian's agricultural terraces and adults 'going gray.' Official records from both worlds show no such event. Emotional beat: the first crack in the official history.

chapters.title: The Vault Below
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She searches the seed vault's founding archives for Meridian's original genetic stock and finds entire decades redacted — by her mother, Adaeze Okonkwo, the vault's previous caretaker. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as burden; suspicion that her family was complicit.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, One Silence
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Flashback structure through Ilsa's adult memories surfacing in dreams: the political fracture that ended Earth–Meridian communication, and the Halcyon's secret mission to broker peace. Emotional beat: grief for a diplomacy that failed before it began.

chapters.title: Gray Fields
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, childlike and fragmentary. Tam remembers hiding in a root cellar while 'the gray rain' fell, watching neighbors dissolve. The detail matches no known weapon — except one entry in the vault's sealed chemical index. Emotional beat: terror rendered through a child's vocabulary.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Daughter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She deciphers her mother's private logs and learns Adaeze helped design the memory-erasure protocol that scrubbed Meridian's records from every shared archive. Emotional beat: betrayal, then a colder resolve — she will finish what her mother buried.

chapters.title: Summons
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Both Earth's Directorate and Meridian's remnant council demand custody of the Halcyon children. Marguerite invokes the vault's ancient neutrality charter to keep them, making herself the enemy of both governments. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Second Ship
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Long-range sensors detect another vessel inbound from Meridian — military, fast, and broadcasting a demand: return the children or be sterilized like the rest. Emotional beat: countdown begins; safety was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Seeds as Evidence
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She realizes the vault's seed samples from Meridian carry isotopic traces of the gray agent — physical proof the massacre happened. But accessing the deep archive requires biometric keys held by the dead. Emotional beat: hope entangled with impossibility.

chapters.title: Tam Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Under stress, Tam's memories accelerate, unlocking not just the massacre but the identity of the orderer: Director-General Cass, now Earth's most beloved statesman. Emotional beat: innocence forced to carry unbearable knowledge.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa confronts a visiting Directorate envoy and recognizes him as Cass's fixer, the man who administered the reversal treatment aboard the Halcyon. He offers the crew amnesty in exchange for the data cores. Emotional beat: temptation and contempt in equal measure.

chapters.title: Mother's Key
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In her mother's final log, hidden inside a seed packet of extinct wheat, Marguerite finds the biometric key — and a confession: Adaeze kept proof of the massacre all along but lacked the courage to release it. Emotional beat: forgiveness arriving too late to matter, yet changing everything.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The Directorate seizes the relay network; the Meridian warship enters orbit; the vault goes dark. Marguerite seals the children in the deep archive as soldiers breach the outer levels. Emotional beat: siege claustrophobia; the past literally closing in.

chapters.title: The Gray Rain, Again
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The boarding team deploys a localized memory-erasure field. Ilsa sacrifices herself in the archive antechamber, holding the door long enough for Marguerite and the children to reach the core vault. Emotional beat: heroic loss; the cost of witness made flesh.

chapters.title: Everything the Seeds Know
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Inside the deepest vault, she initiates the archive's dormant broadcast system — designed to reseed worlds, repurposed to reseed memory. The full record of the massacre, her mother's confession, and the isotopic evidence begin uploading to every relay in range. Emotional beat: terrible triumph.

chapters.title: Cass Descends
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Cass). The Director-General arrives personally, offering Marguerite restoration of the vault's funding, her mother's honor, and the children's futures if she halts the broadcast. His charm is genuine, which makes it worse. Emotional beat: power's seduction at its most persuasive.

chapters.title: The Vote of Children
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Cass demands the children testify that they remember nothing. Instead, one by one, they stand and recite what they saw — names, dates, the smell of the gray rain. Tam speaks last, naming Cass himself. Emotional beat: the powerless becoming the unanswerable.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With Cass's forces storming the vault, Marguerite completes the transmission and triggers the archive's failsafe, incinerating the seed stock rather than let it be weaponized. The truth floods both worlds' networks simultaneously. Emotional beat: climax — everything burning so nothing is lost.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Days later: Cass arrested by his own Directorate as the evidence spreads; the Meridian warship stands down; Earth and Meridian open their first channel in forty years. The children wait for a ship home. Emotional beat: exhausted, fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Grave
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Radiation exposure from the failsafe is fatal. She spends her final weeks planting the last viable seeds in the vault's ruined greenhouse with the children, recording a final message for both worlds about memory as inheritance. Emotional beat: serene acceptance; legacy chosen over survival.

chapters.title: First Contact, Again
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, years later. Now grown, Tam leads the joint Earth–Meridian restoration mission, carrying Marguerite's recorded message and a sapling grown from the greenhouse's surviving seed. The two worlds speak again — carefully, honestly. Emotional beat: resolution; memory planted where silence used to grow.
